title: Direct Current (DC)
content: The direct current is a steady unidirectional current. In a direct current, the electrons flow steadily in the same direction all the time.
e: Direct Current (DC): The direct current is a steady unidirectional current. In a direct current, the electrons flow steadily in the same direction all the time. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

title: Alternating Current (AC)
content: The alternating current is a current that reverses its direction at regular time intervals. In the alternating current the direction of the flow of electrons changes periodically.
e: Alternating Current (AC): The alternating current is a current that reverses its direction at regular time intervals. In the alternating current the direction of the flow of electrons changes periodically. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

title: Electromagnetic Induction
content: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop. This phenomenon is called electromagnetic induction.
e: Electromagnetic Induction: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop. This phenomenon is called electromagnetic induction. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

title: Induced Current
content: The current produced by the electromagnetic induction is called an induced current.
e: Induced Current: The current produced by the electromagnetic induction is called an induced current. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

title: Induced emf
content: The electromotive force (emf) which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced emf.
e: Induced emf: The electromotive force (emf) which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced emf. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

title: Magnetic Flux Density
content: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing perpendicularly through a unit area of material.
e: Magnetic Flux Density: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing perpendicularly through a unit area of material. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

title: Magnetic flux
content: Magnetic flux is a measurement of the total magnetic lines of force which passes through surface area.
e: Magnetic flux is a measurement of the total magnetic lines of force which passes through surface area. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

title: Faraday's Law
content: The magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change magnetic flux through that loop.
e: Faraday's Law: The magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change magnetic flux through that loop. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

title: Lenz's Law
content: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it.
e: Lenz's Law: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

title: AC Generator
content: A generator is an electromagnetic device which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
e: AC Generator: A generator is an electromagnetic device which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field.

title: Transformer
content: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current.
e: Transformer: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

title: Lamination
content: The core of a transformer is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance called lamination.
e: Lamination: The core of a transformer is built up of thin iron sheets of high resistance called lamination. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

title: Primary Coil and Secondary Coil
content: One of coils connected to an alternating voltage source is called the primary coil and is denoted by P. The other coil S called the secondary coil is connected to an electrical device to which electrical power to be supplied.
e: Primary Coil and Secondary Coil: One of coils connected to an alternating voltage source is called the primary coil and is denoted by P. The other coil S called the secondary coil is connected to an electrical device to which electrical power to be supplied. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

title: Eddy Currents
content: In a transformer, the changing magnetic field not only induces currents in the secondary coil, but also currents in the iron core itself. These currents flow in little circles in the iron core and are called eddy currents.
e: Eddy Currents: In a transformer, the changing magnetic field not only induces currents in the secondary coil, but also currents in the iron core itself. These currents flow in little circles in the iron core and are called eddy currents. Primary takes the AC supply; secondary delivers power to the load, with voltages in the turns ratio.

title: Step-down Transformer
content: If the secondary has fewer turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is smaller than the voltage applied to the primary, such a transformer is called a step-down transformer.
e: Step-down Transformer: If the secondary has fewer turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is smaller than the voltage applied to the primary, such a transformer is called a step-down transformer. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

title: Step-up Transformer
content: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is greater than the voltage applied to the primary, such a transformer is called a step-up transformer.
e: Step-up Transformer: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the voltage obtained from the secondary is greater than the voltage applied to the primary, such a transformer is called a step-up transformer. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

title: Efficiency of a Transformer
content: The efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the output power to the input power.
e: Efficiency of a Transformer: The efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the output power to the input power. A transformer needs changing flux, so it works on AC; Vs/Vp follows the turns ratio.

title: Power Circuit (Ring Main Circuit)
content: A power circuit is an electrical system in which distribution points (power sockets) are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit (ring main circuit).
e: Power Circuit (Ring Main Circuit): A power circuit is an electrical system in which distribution points (power sockets) are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit (ring main circuit). A ring main feeds sockets both ways around a loop so cable current is shared.

title: Heating Circuit
content: Heating circuit is for the utilization of appliances such as electric cookers, oven, hot plates, washing machines and dryers.
e: Heating circuit is for the utilization of appliances such as electric cookers, oven, hot plates, washing machines and dryers. As electric cookers, oven, hot plates, washing machines and dryers. Heating Circuit.

title: Circuit Breaker
content: A circuit breaker is used to prevent the overloaded used in electric and electrical appliance for safety reasons. Circuit breaker is an automatic switch which trips (turns OFF) when the current rises above the specified value.
e: Circuit Breaker: A circuit breaker is used to prevent the overloaded used in electric and electrical appliance for safety reasons. Circuit breaker is an automatic switch which trips (turns OFF) when the current rises above the specified value. A breaker is a reusable automatic switch that trips on overload or a short.

title: Earthing
content: Earthing of an electrical appliance is the most important safety precaution. An earthing system (or) grounding system connects specific parts of an electric power system with the ground, typically the earth's conductive surface, for safety and functional purposes.
e: Earthing of an electrical appliance is the most important safety precaution. An earthing system (or) grounding system connects specific parts of an electric power system with the ground, typically the earth's conductive surface, for safety and functional purposes. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live.

title: Live Wire
content: The voltage of live wire goes alternately negative and positive, making the current flow backwards and forwards through the circuit.
e: Live Wire: The voltage of live wire goes alternately negative and positive, making the current flow backwards and forwards through the circuit. The live conductor swings plus and minus and is the dangerous one.

title: Neutral Wire
content: Neutral wire completes the circuit. It is kept at zero voltage by the electricity supply company.
e: Neutral wire completes the circuit. It is kept at zero voltage by the electricity supply company. Neutral is held near zero by the supply company and completes the loop.

title: Earth Wire
content: Earth wire is a safety wire. It connects the metal body of the kettle to earth and stop it becoming live.
e: Earth wire is a safety wire. It connects the metal body of the kettle to earth and stop it becoming live. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live.
